content: {"experiments": [[{"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 2}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 3}], [{"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "put", "connection": "other", "key": "b", "value": 2}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 3}, {"op": "delete", "connection": "other", "key": "b", "value": null}], [{"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 1}, {"op": "begin", "connection": "main", "key": null, "value": null}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 2}, {"op": "put", "connection": "main", "key": "a", "value": 3}, {"op": "rollback", "connection": "main", "key": null, "value": null}]], "purpose": "Separate the three put conflict modes and the three channel definitions. Experiment 1 (three puts on one key, no transaction) distinguishes INSERT OR IGNORE (channel 1, sum 1) from INSERT OR REPLACE / ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (channel 3, sum 3), and separates main-only counters from the main+other counter only weakly. Experiment 2 (writes on both connections plus a delete on other) separates main changes() (counts only main-connection changes) from main total_changes and from main+other total_changes, since the other-connection put and delete contribute only to the latter two. Experiment 3 (two puts inside a transaction that is rolled back) tests whether the channel counts rolled-back direct changes: changes() and total_changes still count the two attempted puts, while a committed-effect counter would not, and it also confirms whether the trigger fires per attempted insert (log rows) versus per committed row, which the committed-state reader cannot see."}
